from.place: ## Proof, step (b) Essential surjectivity: algebraization through formal glueing, specifically the torsion-extension descent used in Proposition 05ER

title: Extensions of a cyclic ideal-power quotient descend over a flat neighbourhood
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], let $I\subseteq R$ be a finitely generated ideal such that $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism, let $n\ge1$, and let $N$ be an $R$-module. Put $C=R/I^n$ and $C_S=C\otimes_RS$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. For every short exact sequence of $S$-modules $0\to N\otimes_RS\xrightarrow{a}T\xrightarrow{b}C_S\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], there are an exact sequence of $R$-modules $0\to N\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q}C\to0$ and an $S$-linear isomorphism $E\otimes_RS\simeq T$ commuting with both maps from $N\otimes_RS$ and to $C_S$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EG (lemma-neighbourhood-extensions, line 24477), proof after 'reduce to the case where M = R/I^n': the diagram from Lemma 05EE and annihilation by Lemma 05EF

proof.text: Put J = I^n. Lift 1 tensor 1 through b to tau. Since b(r tau) = 0 for r in J, exactness and injectivity of a give the unique R-linear map d : J -> S tensor N with a(d(r)) = r tau. This uses the inverse of a onto its range, which is uniquely determined.
Apply the ideal-power Hom lifting lemma to d. Obtain l : J -> N and m with 1 tensor l(r) = d(r) + r m. Set tau-prime = tau + a(m); then b(tau-prime) = 1 tensor 1 and a(1 tensor l(r)) = r tau-prime.

Construct E = (N direct-sum R)/range(r -> (l(r),-r)), j(p) = [(p,0)], q([(p,r)]) = r mod J. The quotient map q is well-defined. A relation with second coordinate zero has r = 0, proving j injective. If r is in J, [(p,r)] = j(p+l(r)); this proves exactness. Every quotient element r mod J is q([(0,r)]), proving surjectivity.
The map (p,r) -> a(1 tensor p) + r tau-prime kills the relations; descend to g : E -> T and extend scalars to theta0 : S tensor E -> T. On pure tensors, theta0 j_S = a and b theta0 = q_S.

Flat tensor exactness gives ker q_S = range j_S; tensor right exactness gives q_S surjective. If theta0(z) = 0, then q_S(z) = 0, so z = j_S(p); a(p) = 0 implies p = 0 and z = 0. For t in T choose e with q_S(e) = b(t), then t-theta0(e) = a(p) by exactness. Thus theta0(j_S(p)+e) = t. Use its bijectivity to obtain theta, with both commuting squares proved above.
